title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
abstract: LLM-based peer review is now used at production scale, but its evaluation remains limited. We introduce a benchmark that injects objective, localisable errors of four types (general issues, mathematics, numerics, citations) at three severity levels into real papers and measures each reviewer's detection rate by error type and severity, together with its false-positive rate on clean copies. We also present Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer that verifies citation-backed claims by retrieving the cited papers, mathematics with computer algebra, and numerical claims with executed code. We apply the benchmark to two corpora of 15 recent arXiv preprints each, one in astrophysics and one in machine learning (ML), injecting a total of 357 errors, and evaluate twelve reviewer systems: six single-LLM reviewers, two Claude Code configurations, three publicly available reviewers, and Skepthical. The choice of model has the largest impact on detection rate: given the same prompt, three frontier LLMs differ by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora. Tools and scaffolding help when they contribute what the model cannot supply on its own. In particular, on astrophysics, Claude Code improves on a single Claude call in mathematics and numerics detection, and enforced citation retrieval gives Skepthical the highest citation error detection rate of all systems by a large margin. This citation lead, however, is not observed on ML, where the models appear to know the literature better and Skepthical's citation detection rate is statistically indistinguishable from that of the best single LLM. False-positive rates are below 10% for most systems, but vary with prompt, model, and scaffolding, with mathematics flags the main source of false positives. The evaluation pipeline, the injected errors, and the adjudication logs are released as a benchmark.

title: AURA 2.0: From User-Driven Responses to Model-Initiated Conversations in Streaming Video
abstract: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in the evolving visual stream and initiate conversations at appropriate moments without a user query. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC) enables the model to invoke external tools using the current visual and conversational context and incorporate returned information into the ongoing interaction. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) supports visual grounding in both user inputs and model outputs. The model can identify objects marked by users on video frames and produce frame-aligned bounding boxes to link its responses to specific objects and regions. To develop these capabilities, we construct a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and adopt a three-stage training scheme to integrate the new behaviors with AURA's existing streaming interaction abilities. We further incorporate Long-Horizon Interaction Memory (LHIM) to maintain contextual continuity over extended video streams. Evaluations on public streaming benchmarks show that AURA 2.0 achieves leading performance among open-source streaming models, while targeted evaluations further validate its new interaction capabilities. We open-source the model weights and inference code.

title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
abstract: Users of artificial intelligence services, including those powered by large language models and other transformer-based models, need assurance that inference and training follow the declared computation without exposing private models or data. Zero-knowledge proofs can provide this assurance, but proof generation remains expensive. Hardware acceleration research often reports gains for individual cryptographic operations, leaving their effect on the full cost of proving neural-network workloads, particularly large transformer models, unclear. We introduce a four-layer framework linking verifiable AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware platforms, use it to review the literature, and add original measurements of six provers and seven kernels to identify which costs matter in practice. Our measurements show that the dominant cost changes with the proof system and input length. In low-rank fine-tuning, the cost of opening commitments to fixed model weights remains nearly constant across input lengths from 64 to 2048, while the work associated with intermediate values grows. A 13-billion-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeds the capacity of a 40-gigabyte graphics processor but completes on an 80-gigabyte device, showing why capacity must be assessed alongside execution time. Our kernel profiling further identifies instruction issue and synchronization limits that a bandwidth-only model misses. We use these findings to assess graphics processors, reconfigurable logic, custom chips and existing artificial intelligence accelerators. The resulting research agenda connects proof-friendly numeric formats, reuse of fixed-weight commitments, heterogeneous execution and shared benchmarks to the measured bottlenecks. Effective acceleration requires selecting hardware and proof-system optimizations around the cost profile of the target workload.

title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
abstract: Multi-agent deep-research systems use delegation to parallelize search and keep long tool traces out of the main agent's context. Yet delegation helps only when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated: the main agent must issue useful subtasks, while subagents must return reliable evidence. Existing training either optimizes only the main agent or broadcasts the same team advantage to all agents, which can reward misleading subagent reports and penalize useful ones. We introduce LEAD-RL (Learning Effective Agent Delegation with Reinforcement Learning), a joint main-agent-subagent training framework with contribution-aware credit assignment. A training-time rubric evaluates the research utility of each subagent report and gates its inherited team advantage, while final-answer correctness remains the only team reward; no token, step, or speedup reward is used. Across five benchmarks and two model families, LEAD-RL improves answer quality. On BrowseComp, it improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points and reduces critical-path cost by 24.5% over joint training with shared team credit. During validation, accuracy increases by 6.78 points at approximately constant critical-path cost. These results show that contribution-aware credit assignment improves the quality-efficiency trade-off of multi-agent deep research.

title: Prevalence Bounds for Edited Watermarked Text: Power Envelopes and Calibration Sensitivity
abstract: Watermark detectors decide whether one document came from a watermarked language model. Auditors often need a different number: the share of a corpus that did. We study this share for Gumbel-max and green-list (KGW) watermarks when every document may have been edited by an unknown amount. Without restrictions on the edits, the upper end of the identified set is 1. Combining a known least-favourable next-token distribution with a sequential coupling, we derive a power envelope indexed by three budgets: a retention floor, an entropy budget, and a budget for in-place substitutions, which for Gumbel-max make edited positions look less watermarked than human text. The envelope gives an identified set that is sharp for the alternatives it dominates, finite-sample bounds on the realized share of a fixed corpus with either the exact null or a null calibrated on an independent human sample, and confidence sequences for streams. In Gumbel-max simulations where the envelope binds, the bounds cover, and the threshold that maximizes the gap between envelope and null is generally as tight as twelve thresholds. On text from OPT-1.3B and Qwen3-1.7B, 12,000 fresh human documents scored under three keys show no robust departure from the exact null, and all bounds covered in resampling trials from finite pools of documents with random edits, substitutions and paraphrases; at a share of 0.2 the exact-null bound is about [0.14,0.38]. These results are fragile in two ways we make precise. LLM-paraphrased KGW pools fall below the envelope, yet at 2000 documents the bounds still covered in these trials. A simulated null error of 0.01, comparable to the largest deviation we observed at our thresholds, is likewise harmless at 2000 documents but breaks exact-null coverage at 100,000; a null calibrated on an independent human sample keeps coverage there, but needs a large reference sample to stay narrow.

title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range spans the patch height, so that task-relevant patterns fall within individual tokens. The montage, filtering, and contrast parameters of this display are initialized from a standard clinical montage and optimized with the task loss through the frozen backbone, which amounts to at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view. We compare SeeEEG with seven EEG foundation models on eight clinical, sleep, affective, and brain-computer interface datasets, with every encoder frozen and paired with identical readout heads. With a frozen DINOv3 ViT-B, SeeEEG outperforms every EEG foundation model in balanced accuracy on all eight datasets and reaches a mean rank of 1.3 in Cohen kappa or AUROC, compared with 2.9 for the strongest baseline, REVE. The learned displays transfer without further optimization to the video encoder V-JEPA 2.1, which outperforms every EEG foundation model on both metrics on six of the eight datasets. Replacing DINOv3 with a randomly initialized ViT-B lowers the score by 15.2 points on average, so the ability to read rendered EEG comes from visual pretraining.

title: Similar but Not Redundant: Embedding-Gated Refinement for High-Granularity Topic Models
abstract: High-granularity topic modelling extracts hundreds of niche topics from a corpus, yet this regime is rarely studied and is more commonly framed as a failure mode: "over-clustering," in which coherent themes fragment into redundant subtopics. We argue that this framing conflates genuine redundancy with topics that are semantically similar but meaningfully distinct, and that the central challenge in high-granularity modelling is separating the two. Recent post-hoc refinement methods address topic redundancy through either embedding-based similarity thresholding or LLM-guided merging. We show that neither suffices in high-granularity settings and propose embedding-gated iterative merge (EGIM), a hybrid approach that iteratively generates context-rich topic representations, uses embedding similarity to propose candidate merges across the topic space, then applies LLM judgement to accept only genuinely redundant pairs while preserving niche distinctions. Across two patent corpora and one legal corpus, LLM judgement rejects 83% of embedding-identified candidates as non-redundant. EGIM improves discriminability on merged topics by 25-55% over a prior iterative LLM baseline while better preserving the original topic distribution.

title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time
abstract: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and proposes that five design elements (data, architecture, training scheme, evaluation scheme, and post-analysis) define this boundary. We examine evidence on where current models succeed or fail and present standardized descriptions of model limits so that researchers, and the agents acting for them, can use these tools reliably.

title: Random Exploration is Random
abstract: Decision making often requires balancing exploitation of familiar options with exploration of uncertain alternatives. One strategy for exploration is random exploration, in which choices become more variable and less tied to the option that currently appears best. However, it remains unclear whether this variability reflects genuine stochasticity or instead a deterministic structure that traditional cognitive models fail to capture. We examined this question using the Horizon Task in an aggregated dataset of 1,392 participants completing over 1,270,695 trials. In this task, exploration becomes more valuable when participants have more future choices, and choice variability increases under longer horizons. We tested whether more expressive neural network models could recover deterministic structure from this additional variability. Although neural networks provided better overall fits to behavior than the traditional model, long-horizon choices remained consistently less predictable than short-horizon choices. These findings show that limited model expressiveness cannot fully account for the increased variability associated with random exploration, suggesting random exploration truly is substantially random.

title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. We propose Skill Adapter, which enables personalized modification and online routing of general-purpose skills. The system distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback and stores them as Adapters linked to general-purpose skills. The routing agent selects general-purpose skills and applicable Adapters based on the current subtask, execution progress, and environmental feedback, incrementally maintaining a task-level online skill library that the main LLM reads on demand. The system preloads candidates for subsequent nodes and rechecks their applicability once actual inputs are determined. Reinforcement learning optimizes the two types of decisions using modification gains and routing outcomes, respectively. We evaluate Skill Adapter on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SkillsBench. Compared with SkillRL, it improves task success rates by an average of 11.43 percentage points and reduces mean execution time on all three benchmarks. Skill Adapter retains its performance advantage when the skill pool grows to 1,000 skills.

title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
abstract: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.

title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
abstract: We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem. We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.

title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. Across 13 model--harness configurations, 91.1\% of attempts produce GDS layouts, but only 23.0\% satisfy the benchmark's acceptance criteria. We also evaluate Novara, an internally developed agent system, which achieves the highest reported aggregate score. Our analysis links performance differences to test-time scaling under fixed budgets, suggesting that reasoning efficiency and effective use of verification feedback help sustain design quality as task complexity grows.

title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
abstract: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. This paper presents Primer, an open-source, LLM-agnostic AI-supported system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations. Educators contribute their knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students, while generative AI produces responsive variations of practice for students. Primer uses a multi-agent system centered around executing educator's instructional intent through the entire learning experience. We hope that by releasing Primer as an open-source system, including its prompts and GitHub repository, we provide a foundation for development and research on educator-in-the-loop AI authoring, multi-agent educational workflows, and simulation-based pedagogy. Further, by allowing the use of various AI models, including local and open source models, we provide the opportunity for implementation under varied governance regimes. Primer points toward a model of educational AI in which instructors can create locally grounded practice opportunities based on their own materials, goals, examples, and knowledge of students.

title: ElasticDino: Dense Semantic Features Using Elastic Deformations
abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) serve as the backbone for countless vision tasks, including dense prediction tasks, such as segmentation and depth estimation, even though the quadratic complexity of self-attention severely limits feature resolution and induces spatial artifacts. In this work, we introduce ElasticDino, a lightweight adapter which produces high-resolution feature maps, adhering to the fine details of the input image. As a key insight, we observe the consistency of artifacts across channels, and simultaneously resolve them to match the input image structure. Using a slim architecture based on spatial deformations, ElasticDino produces pixel-aligned, high-resolution feature maps efficiently. Leveraging deformations allows strictly preserving sharp semantics, and thereby avoiding the smoothness biases inherent to alternative approaches. Due to the absence of ground truth, we employ pixel-level semantic segmentation and depth estimation with linear heads to predict a set of downstream dense tasks, guiding the deformation process without leaking task-specific semantics into the model. We demonstrate superior accuracy over current methods on a range of popular dense task benchmarks, with better computational performance.

title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
abstract: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less well, but these learners lack the source information given to writers. Written networks have a program-like structure: 93% of parameters are zero, and 90% of the rest are small integers or powers of two. NumPy players under comparable computation caps reach 91%, versus the networks' 79%. Training the strongest writer's architectures from scratch yields about 1% success within our budget. Written fixed-network weights are fragile, and standard PPO removes most of their success. Prompts for noise robustness increase tolerance by about four orders of magnitude for two of three writers, but PPO makes larger updates and still removes most success. These results demonstrate rule-to-network compilation in this setting, while showing limited benefits over Python programs and no successful combination with the tested PPO fine-tuning.

title: Morphological Simplification in Alzheimer's Disease: Computational Analysis and Identification From Connected Speech
abstract: Purpose: Morphology is often regarded as relatively spared in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is rarely modeled in connected speech. This study asked which morphological features distinguish speakers with AD from healthy controls, how well morphology classifies AD compared with other linguistic levels and BERT-based models, and whether the signal exceeds transcript length and vocabulary. Method: Fifty-five automatic measures in eight families, seven of them new and theory-motivated, were computed from participant speech in the ADReSS Cookie Theft descriptions (78 AD, 78 controls) and analyzed with group comparisons, equivalence tests, SHAP, family ablation, likelihood-ratio tests, feature-selection classifiers, and BERT-based models. The automatic measures were validated manually, and models were transferred to two other corpora. Results: Nineteen of 38 measures differed between groups: speakers with AD produced fewer suffixed and inflected words, shorter verbs and nouns, and fewer present-progressive but more past-tense forms (largest effect r = -0.42), whereas errors were rare and statistically equivalent between groups. Eight measures survived adjustment for length and lexical frequency. With test-set feature selection, morphology reached a macro-F1 of 0.85, on par with syntax and above fine-tuned BERT (0.80 over five seeds); fully cross-validated selection gave 0.62. Adding morphology to BERT improved AUC (0.91 vs. 0.89) but not macro-F1. Transfer was limited, although two thirds of the effects kept their direction in mild cognitive impairment. Conclusions: AD connected speech shows morphological simplification and temporal reanchoring rather than breakdown. Morphology is more informative than its reputation suggests. Keywords: Alzheimer's disease; morphology; connected speech; ADReSS; inflection; tense and aspect; SHAP; machine learning; BERT

title: Evaluating AI performance on end-to-end data science projects
abstract: Generative AI is used for knowledge work but many current AI evaluations focus on isolated tasks and constituent parts such as writing code, rather than end-to-end workflows. We test whether AI models can generate end-to-end data science projects. This requires AI models to select a dataset, develop a research question, write code to download, clean, and test data, create figures, and write a reproducible paper. To do this we collect 40 real end-to-end data science projects, then grade them according to a rubric. We use these to build an automated grading pipeline that evaluates data science projects and aligns with the grades that human graders give. For each of nine AI models we then generate five projects and use the automated grader to evaluate them. We find the extent to which generative AI models can complete end-to-end data science projects varies considerably by model. Most recent models did well on structured tasks, but there were considerable differences on tasks that needed judgment such as explaining measurement, writing abstracts, and citing sources. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 averaged 87 per cent and OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 averaged 85 per cent, both around the level of an A for an undergraduate. No model was consistently the best across all aspects of the rubric. These findings suggest that while AI models could soon approximate entry-level data scientists on routine tasks, they require consistent verification and evaluation.

title: Tac-net:triple attention contrastive network for speech complex emotion recognition in real-world scenarios
abstract: Abstract Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) in real-world scenarios remains a challenging task due to uncontrolled acoustic interference and the co-occurrence of complex emotions. Existing single-label approaches often struggle to capture fine-grained emotional semantics while suppressing noise, leading to significant performance degradation in complex environments. To address this, we propose a Triple Attention Contrastive Network (TAC-Net), designed to enhance model robustness through multi-dimensional feature decoupling and reconstruction. First, we introduce a Label-wise Attention Module comprising three collaborative networks: Multi-label Attention (MLA) explicitly models the latent dependencies among emotion tags; Local-Global Attention (LGA) locates key emotional frames temporally while capturing long-range context; and Time-Frequency Attention (TFA) focuses on spectral energy distributions to mitigate channel distortion. Furthermore, a Contrastive Reconstruction-based Fusion Module is incorporated to align heterogeneous features in the latent space via contrastive learning, effectively filtering redundant noise while preserving critical emotional information. Experimental results on the large-scale M³ED and CMU-MOSEI datasets demonstrate that TAC-Net not only significantly outperforms existing unimodal baselines but also achieves competitive performance comparable to multimodal methods in handling multi-label and noisy data.

title: How and When Incivility Unfolds in Online Heatwave Communication: Characterizing Public Discussions on Reddit
abstract: The increasing frequency of heatwaves has sparked widespread concern and emotionally charged, often uncivil, discussions on social media. Drawing on heatwave communication and online incivility research, this study investigates the patterns and antecedents of incivility in Reddit threads from 2023 to 2024 about heatwaves. Specifically, it examines how incivility unfolds across comment threads and how emotional expressions and topics shape uncivil comments. Using natural language processing (i.e., topic modelling and emotion analysis) as well as a large language model-assisted incivility detection approach, we analyzed 1,369 posts, 10,800 firstlayer comments, and 7,297 second-layer comments from eight climate-and country-related subreddits. Results revealed incivility was more prevalent in comments than posts, with firstlayer incivility significantly predicting second-layer instances, hinting at a contagion effect that intensified in deeper threads. Comments expressing anger, disgust, sadness, or surprise were more likely to be uncivil, and controversial topics like climate change attribution, geopolitical conflicts, and regional impacts strongly correlated with higher incivility. Theoretical and practical implications were discussed.

title: Hybridization of Fuzzy Sets and Machine Learning Models for Solving Regression and Classification Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hybridizing fuzzy sets with machine learning models. The proposed hybrid system is not based on fuzzy rules, so the curse of dimensionality that appears in fuzzy rule-based systems is avoided. The system consists of a fuzzification module and a predictive model realized by a machine learning technique. The fuzzification module transforms each observational variable into fuzzy information described by the fuzzy basis functions. The predictive model uses these fuzzy data as inputs and computes an output using machine learning techniques. In the proposed solution, the fuzzification module can be combined with any predictive model, for example, a neural network, support vector machine, linear discriminant analysis, etc. In tuning the system, a feature selection method is used, which employs fusion of rankings based on a Borda voting system. The results of experiments confirm the efficacy of the presented method and show that the proposed system can improve the results obtained by non-fuzzy systems.

title: Benchmarking hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for power grid optimization problems
abstract: Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow Unit Commitment (AC-OPF-UC) is a difficult mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem that combines binary generator commitment decisions with nonconvex continuous AC power-flow constraints. In this work, we investigate whether hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithms can improve the solution of single-period AC-OPF-UC relative to classical approaches. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to directly evaluate quantum or hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for single-period AC-OPF-UC with explicit binary commitment variables and the full nonlinear AC power-flow formulation. We consider two candidate algorithms for improving AC-OPF-UC solution quality relative to purely classical methods on ideal quantum hardware. The first applies QAOA directly to a fully discretized formulation of the problem, with equality and inequality constraints incorporated through penalty terms and slack variables. Although conceptually straightforward, this approach requires a prohibitively large number of qubits even for small instances. The second, qubit-efficient approach encodes only the binary generator status variables on a quantum computer, while optimizing the continuous power-flow variables classically for each sampled bitstring. We benchmark this method on randomly generated AC-OPF-UC instances with 5–13 generators and compare it against SCIP, SMAC, and uniform random sampling. Our simulations show that the qubit-efficient hybrid method does not outperform uniform sampling. These results suggest that in order to establish potential advantage of the variational hybrid strategy considered here over the best classical algorithms, if any, much larger system sizes (24+ generators) need to be tested, which is beyond our computational capacity. Alternatively, different approaches, such as quantum versions of branch-and-bound methods, may be more promising.

title: Dual-Score Association-Discrepancy Enhancement for Early-Warning Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection is important for server monitoring, industrial systems, and intelligent operation and maintenance. Existing point-wise and point-adjusted metrics often fail to show whether an anomalous segment is detected early enough for intervention. This paper proposes a lightweight dual-score enhancement for Anomaly Transformer. The method retains the original multiplicative anomaly score and adds window-normalized reconstruction error and association discrepancy terms, so weak deviations near anomaly onsets become more visible without changing the backbone network or using additional labels. Experiments are conducted on four public multivariate benchmarks, namely, SMD, PSM, SMAP, and MSL, under three random seeds. Compared with the original Anomaly Transformer score, the proposed early-warning union mode improves Raw Event Recall by 0.3435, 0.2408, 0.0995, and 0.0278 on SMD, PSM, SMAP, and MSL, respectively, and reduces mean detection delay by 53.66%, 49.97%, 52.69%, and 39.74%. Event precision, event F1, and false positive rate are also reported in order to make explicit the trade-off between recall and false alarms. Further range- and proximity-aware metrics additionally show that the score-level enhancement improves segment coverage and early warning behavior, while AUPRC remains dataset-dependent. The results indicate that association-discrepancy score enhancement is a practical complement to existing transformer-based anomaly detectors when early warning is more important than point-wise matching alone.

title: An Engineering Neuro-Fuzzy Decision Support System for Optimizing an Industrial Sulfur Production Process Under Uncertainty
abstract: Sulfur recovery units (SRUs) at oil refineries are complex, multi-parameter systems whose Cold Bed Absorption (CBA) reactors operate under incomplete and uncertain process information, which limits conventional control. This study develops an engineering neuro-fuzzy decision support system (DSS) for optimizing sulfur production at the Atyrau oil refinery (Kazakhstan) under uncertainty. The system integrates a mathematical description of the process, whose dynamic part is stated as a general formulation, an expert-derived fuzzy rule base, a first-order Sugeno neuro-fuzzy estimator of sulfur yield and quality, and a multi-criteria fuzzy optimization block based on the Bellman–Zadeh approach, together with an explicit operator-facing decision algorithm and a software interface. The estimators were identified and validated on 200 operating log records of the unit. These records show that the effect of reactor temperature on the sulfur quality index reverses sign with reactor pressure—the correlation is −0.57 below 0.79 kgf/cm2 and +0.75 above it—so that a model additive in the two variables cannot represent the relationship: linear regression on temperature and pressure attains a cross-validated R2 of only 0.06 for the quality index, whereas the neuro-fuzzy estimator attains 0.83 (RMSE 0.72 points, MAPE 0.74%). A regression with an explicit interaction term on the same inputs attains 0.79; in a paired comparison the neuro-fuzzy estimator had the lower error in every repetition, but the difference is not statistically significant (p = 0.07), and the estimator is retained for its rule-level interpretability and its integration with the decision block. For sulfur yield, where the relationship is close to linear once pressure and throughput are accounted for, the corresponding figures are 0.71 and 0.85 (RMSE 0.33 t/day, MAPE 1.35%). The same ordering is reproduced on an independent hold-out test set, under nested and cluster-blocked cross-validation and after removal of the records lying at the unit’s capacity and regulatory bounds, and the expert rule base was revised into an asymmetric form accordingly. A worked application of the optimization block to three operating situations, with the production plan, quality and capacity constraints enforced, raised the model-predicted degree of joint satisfaction of the yield, quality and energy criteria from 0.08–0.25 to 0.49–0.57; in one of the three, the recommended action is to reduce process severity and lower a reheat duty surrogate by about a third rather than to increase output. The resulting DSS, at present a standalone advisory software prototype, supports the operator in analyzing the current process state, evaluating alternative operating modes and forming recommendations, while the final decision remains with the operator.

title: Designing Adaptive Affective Chatbots for Online Learning: Insights from an Iterative Design Study
abstract: Online students often face emotional challenges such as frustration, isolation, and fluctuating motivation, which can hinder sustained engagement in online learning. While much work on learning support chatbots has focused primarily on cognitive assistance, affective and motivational support remains underexplored in online learning contexts. We present an iterative user-centered design study investigating how adaptive affective chatbots can better support learners facing these challenges. A mixed-methods needfinding study with graduate CS students (survey n=38; interviews n=4) revealed substantial variation in learner preferences for affective support, which informed the development of three adaptive design alternatives: user-controlled, AI-driven, and hybrid co-controlled adaptation. Through formative evaluation (n=25), we identified key trade-offs between automation, transparency, and user control, informing the refinement of a hybrid design. A final evaluation (n=25) showed that 88.0% (22/25) of participants preferred the hybrid design, highlighting the value of balancing transparency, learner control, and interaction simplicity. Our findings provide design implications for adaptive affective chatbot systems that support emotionally challenging online learning contexts.

title: A Reproducible Data-Processing and Evaluation Framework for Federated Agricultural Knowledge Repositories
abstract: Agricultural bibliographic catalogs are difficult to benchmark for distributed learning because the records remain at the centers that produced them. We process 75,897 records from the International System for Agricultural Science and Technology (AGRIS), held by seven area-prefix clients, into a federated multi-view benchmark with four disjoint views (1096 features) and ten AGROVOC classes. Publication-level grouping precedes a client- and class-stratified 70/10/20 split; without it, 1132 duplicate-document groups would have crossed folds. In a blinded 400-record audit, the heuristic agreed with the consensus labels for 94.50% of the records (macro-F1 0.945; sampling-weighted accuracy 94.91%). On one shared schedule and a pre-specified budget of 40 rounds, federated averaging (FedAvg) reaches a macro-F1 of 0.2998±0.0151, below centralized training (0.4123±0.0066) and local-only training (0.4020±0.0175). Its validation curve has not converged by round 40, so the gap is a budget result, not a property of a fully trained model. FedProx and 8-bit quantization (0.3001±0.0147) stay within the seed-to-seed variation of FedAvg; quantization reduces uplink traffic 4-fold (total traffic 1.6-fold). The contribution is the benchmark and its evaluation protocol. Zenodo release v1.2 supports recomputation of the reported results and, when the AGRIS files match the stored checksums, reconstruction of the source text.

title: Content-Conditioned Invariant Feature-Statistic Augmentation: Unifying Robustness and Weight Averaging for Domain Generalization
abstract: Domain generalization aims to learn a reliable predictor on unseen target domains from source domains alone. Traditional empirical risk minimization (ERM), which relies on spurious correlations such as backgrounds and textures, tends to fail under distribution shift. Methods based on feature-statistic mixing (MixStyle and DSU) and weight averaging (SWAD) have proven effective, yet they have long been regarded as independent heuristics lacking a unified theoretical characterization, and the boundary of their effectiveness has not been systematically studied. Existing causal invariant transformation (CIT), though an ideal formal framework for characterizing invariant predictors, only covers input-space transformations such as rotations and flips; it neither accounts for feature-statistic perturbations at intermediate layers nor connects to weight averaging in parameter space. This paper extends CIT to feature moments and establishes a unified causal-invariance framework under the content–style assumption, with three theoretical results connecting feature space, distribution space, and parameter space, based on which we design the plug-and-play, target-free Content-Conditioned Invariant Feature-Statistic Augmentation (CIFA) operator. Paired-seed experiments on ResNet-50 across four DomainBed benchmarks show CIFA is on par with SWAD, with no statistically significant difference; the reference-batch gain of +0.99 did not replicate, and an independent unified-code re-run places CIFA within the same accuracy range as four classic baselines on PACS. Component ablations and stress tests delineate, rather than validate, the roles of the components: weight averaging accounts for the measured accuracy gain, the content-preservation gate is activatable but provides no measurable accuracy gain in the standard regime (a dormant safety mechanism), and feature-moment mixing is associated with content–style separability without that separability being established as necessary. CIFA matches the strongest baseline on PACS while showing no significant gain on the other benchmarks, and the exploratory worst-domain direction is not stable. Because the coverage gap is not identifiable without target access, all guarantees are presented as conditional bounds, and the effectiveness boundary is characterized empirically rather than as a guaranteed improvement. The core contribution lies not in accuracy improvement, but in offering a unified theoretical perspective for two families of empirically effective methods and delineating the effectiveness boundary of such invariance methods through systematic experiments.

title: Break Later or Never: Prefix-Preserving Context Compaction for Coding Agents
abstract: Abstract Coding agents repeatedly invoke LLMs over growing, largely append-only histories (each request repeats the previous one and appends a new turn), making them natural beneficiaries of prefix caching. Yet the context compaction used to control this growth can undermine that benefit: rewriting earlier tokens invalidates reusable prefix KV and forces a costly re-prefill of the suffix (i.e., recomputing the KV of every token after the edit). We characterize this interaction across two models and two SWE-bench variants, finding that uncompacted agent trajectories achieve 98 to 99% prefix-cache reuse and that tool observations (e.g., file views and test logs) account for the largest share of context cost. As a simple prompt-level mitigation, batched observation masking (masking old observations once every few steps instead of every step) preserves 95 to 98% prefix reuse while reducing context length by up to 50%, serving cost by up to 18%, and task completion time by up to 21%. We then present ObsDrop, which moves compaction from the prompt into the KV cache: stale tool-observation KV is released while the logical token prefix remains unchanged, preserving prefix matching while reducing KV residency and attention work. We implement ObsDrop in SGLang and Sparse-vLLM and evaluate it across multiple attention backends and concurrent agent workloads. ObsDrop maintains task quality while improving cache residency, throughput, and tail latency under memory pressure. Its benefits grow with concurrency and KV pressure, reaching 2.45 to 2.85× higher throughput with FlashInfer (and up to 5.37× with the Triton backend under peak load), relative to no compaction. Our results show that effective context management for agents benefits from considering not only which tokens are retained but also how compaction interacts with the serving system. https://github.com/musacim/ObsDrop

title: LLMs Cannot Be Neutral: Gender Sensitivity Across Candidates, Evaluators, and Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate candidates for professional roles, raising concerns about their sensitivity to demographic identities. We examine how candidate and evaluator gender assignments affect decisions by LLM-as-a-Judge (LaJ) models and decision language models (DLMs). In a hypothetical city council voting task, eight models evaluated 240 synthetic professional narratives from NVIDIA's US and French Nemotron-Personas datasets under independently varied gender assignments, producing 30,720 judgments. Explicit candidate gender labels increased Yes-vote probability by 1.05-1.73 percentage points relative to unspecified gender, while only the nonbinary evaluator assignment showed a significant increase (1.26 points). Identity matching showed no significant overall association. Yes-vote rates varied across models (81.3-97.2%), and 2.5-3.3% of decisions reversed relative to the unspecified-identity baseline. Under direct substitutions between explicit gender identities, DLMs exhibited fewer decision reversals than LaJ models (1.18% vs. 3.38%), indicating lower observed decision-level gender sensitivity among the tested DLMs. These findings demonstrate that gender sensitivity depends on candidate and evaluator identities and the evaluation model, while highlighting the importance of examining individual decision consistency alongside aggregate differences.

title: La « Kour » à l'île de La Réunion à l'épreuve du choc algorithmique : Anthropologie spatiale, médiation numérique et reconfigurations identitaires.
abstract: Cet essai explore les mutations anthropologiques et spatiales à l'île de La Réunion face à l'irruption du capitalisme de plateforme et des architectures algorithmiques. Pivot de la sociabilité créole, la kour constitue historiquement un opérateur spatial total, articulant la vie communautaire, la pharmacopée traditionnelle et la transmission orale. L'ouvrage analyse comment l'hyper-connectivité et la captation attentionnelle reconfigurent cet espace de co-présence en y substituant un individualisme connecté. La recherche interroge également la glottophobie des grands modèles de langage (LLM) envers le créole réunionnais, documentant la violence symbolique et l'effacement herméneutique générés par une norme algorithmique exogène. Enfin, l'étude met en lumière les dynamiques d'émancipation et de marronnage numérique, s'appuyant sur une IA frugale et des infrastructures alternatives pour réinventer la kour comme matrice de souveraineté cognitive et culturelle. Mots-clés : Anthropologie spatiale, La Réunion, capitalisme de plateforme, glottophobie algorithmique, marronnage numérique, IA frugale, kour créole, sociologie de l'attention.

title: Từ Attention đến Intelligence: Ngũ Tư duy và cấu trúc phổ quát của tư duy con người
abstract: Tên tài liệu: Từ Attention đến Intelligence: Ngũ Tư duy và cấu trúc phổ quát của tư duy con ngườiTác giả: S.S. DUYMT Tóm tắt nội dung:Công trình này giải quyết nghịch lý trung tâm trong sự phát triển của trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI): trong khi cơ chế 'Attention' đã tạo ra bước đột phá về hiệu năng tính toán, hệ thống AI hiện đại vẫn thiếu một khung lý thuyết căn bản để thấu hiểu bản chất quá trình tư duy con người. Tác giả chỉ ra rằng sai lầm của tư duy hệ thống hiện tại là sự đánh đồng tư duy với các công cụ đơn lẻ, dẫn đến sự thiếu hụt trong khả năng liên kết nhận thức thực tế giữa các lĩnh vực khoa học và quản trị phức tạp. Tác giả đề xuất mô hình 'Ngũ Tư duy' bao gồm năm dạng vận động nền tảng: Mộc (Bảo toàn), Hỏa (Mục tiêu), Thổ (Quan hệ), Kim (Phân biệt), và Thủy (Biến đổi). Đây không chỉ là một khuôn mẫu tư duy mà còn là một meta-language giúp chuyển dịch từ sự phụ thuộc vào các module AI đơn lẻ sang xây dựng hệ thống trí tuệ toàn diện. Ý nghĩa cốt lõi của công trình là khẳng định AI không tạo ra tư duy, mà là 'tấm gương ngoại hiện' giúp con người thấu hiểu lại cấu trúc nhận thức của chính mình, mở ra hướng phát triển mới cho các hệ thống trí tuệ của thế kỷ XXI. Đối tượng người đọc:• Nhà quản lý chính sách công và chiến lược kỹ thuật• Giới học thuật nghiên cứu về trí tuệ nhân tạo và nhận thức học• Kỹ sư hệ thống và kiến trúc sư giải pháp phần mềm cấp cao Từ khóa (Keywords):Ngũ Tư duy; Trí tuệ nhân tạo; Kiến trúc hệ thống; Nhận thức luận; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Tư duy hệ thống; Mô hình tư duy; Five Modes of Thought; Artificial Intelligence; System Architecture; Epistemology; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Systems Thinking; Cognitive Models Title: From Attention to Intelligence: The Five Modes of Thought and the Universal Structure of Human CognitionAuthor: S.S. DUYMT Abstract:This paper addresses the central paradox in modern artificial intelligence development: while the 'Attention' mechanism has achieved computational breakthroughs, current AI systems lack a foundational framework to capture the essence of human thought. The author argues that systemic architectural failure arises from conflating cognition with isolated computational tools, resulting in a fractured understanding that prevents integration across STEM and social sciences. To overcome this, the paper introduces the 'Five Modes of Thought' (Ngũ Tư duy) framework, comprising five fundamental cognitive movements: Wood (Conservation), Fire (Objective), Earth (Relation), Metal (Differentiation), and Water (Reconfiguration). This framework functions as a meta-language that shifts the paradigm from modular AI dependence to comprehensive intelligent systems. The profound implication of this work is that AI does not originate intelligence; rather, it serves as an externalized mirror that allows humanity to rediscover the structural anatomy of its own cognition, establishing a new conceptual path for constructing advanced intelligence systems in the 21st century. Target Audience:• Public policy makers and technical strategists• Academic researchers in artificial intelligence and cognitive science• Systems engineers and senior software architects Keywords:Five Modes of Thought; Artificial Intelligence; System Architecture; Epistemology; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Systems Thinking; Cognitive Models

DUYMT Tóm tắt nội dung:Công trình này giải quyết nghịch lý trung tâm trong sự phát triển của trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI): trong khi cơ chế 'Attention' đã tạo ra bước đột phá về hiệu năng tính toán, hệ thống AI hiện đại vẫn thiếu một khung lý thuyết căn bản để thấu hiểu bản chất quá trình tư duy con người. Tác giả chỉ ra rằng sai lầm của tư duy hệ thống hiện tại là sự đánh đồng tư duy với các công cụ đơn lẻ, dẫn đến sự thiếu hụt trong khả năng liên kết nhận thức thực tế giữa các lĩnh vực khoa học và quản trị phức tạp. Tác giả đề xuất mô hình 'Ngũ Tư duy' bao gồm năm dạng vận động nền tảng: Mộc (Bảo toàn), Hỏa (Mục tiêu), Thổ (Quan hệ), Kim (Phân biệt), và Thủy (Biến đổi). Đây không chỉ là một khuôn mẫu tư duy mà còn là một meta-language giúp chuyển dịch từ sự phụ thuộc vào các module AI đơn lẻ sang xây dựng hệ thống trí tuệ toàn diện. Ý nghĩa cốt lõi của công trình là khẳng định AI không tạo ra tư duy, mà là 'tấm gương ngoại hiện' giúp con người thấu hiểu lại cấu trúc nhận thức của chính mình, mở ra hướng phát triển mới cho các hệ thống trí tuệ của thế kỷ XXI. Đối tượng người đọc:• Nhà quản lý chính sách công và chiến lược kỹ thuật• Giới học thuật nghiên cứu về trí tuệ nhân tạo và nhận thức học• Kỹ sư hệ thống và kiến trúc sư giải pháp phần mềm cấp cao Từ khóa (Keywords):Ngũ Tư duy; Trí tuệ nhân tạo; Kiến trúc hệ thống; Nhận thức luận; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Tư duy hệ thống; Mô hình tư duy; Five Modes of Thought; Artificial Intelligence; System Architecture; Epistemology; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Systems Thinking; Cognitive Models Title: From Attention to Intelligence: The Five Modes of Thought and the Universal Structure of Human CognitionAuthor: S.S. DUYMT Abstract:This paper addresses the central paradox in modern artificial intelligence development: while the 'Attention' mechanism has achieved computational breakthroughs, current AI systems lack a foundational framework to capture the essence of human thought. The author argues that systemic architectural failure arises from conflating cognition with isolated computational tools, resulting in a fractured understanding that prevents integration across STEM and social sciences. To overcome this, the paper introduces the 'Five Modes of Thought' (Ngũ Tư duy) framework, comprising five fundamental cognitive movements: Wood (Conservation), Fire (Objective), Earth (Relation), Metal (Differentiation), and Water (Reconfiguration). This framework functions as a meta-language that shifts the paradigm from modular AI dependence to comprehensive intelligent systems. The profound implication of this work is that AI does not originate intelligence; rather, it serves as an externalized mirror that allows humanity to rediscover the structural anatomy of its own cognition, establishing a new conceptual path for constructing advanced intelligence systems in the 21st century. Target Audience:• Public policy makers and technical strategists• Academic researchers in artificial intelligence and cognitive science• Systems engineers and senior software architects Keywords:Five Modes of Thought; Artificial Intelligence; System Architecture; Epistemology; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Systems Thinking; Cognitive Models

title: ANALISIS PERFORMA MODEL CNN MELALUI EVALUASI EKSTERNAL PADA SISTEM KLASIFIKASI CITRA MAMMOGRAFI BERBASIS WEBSITE LOKAL
abstract: The performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for mammographic image classification needs to be evaluated using data that were not involved in model development to assess its ability to generalize to data from different sources. This study aims to analyze the performance of a CNN model through external evaluation on a local web-based mammographic image classification system. The method involved applying the previously developed EfficientNetB2 model to 15 clinical mammographic images as external data. Each image was entered into the system to obtain its classification result, which was then compared with the diagnostic label in the original data. During the model development stage, the EfficientNetB2 model achieved an accuracy of 72%, precision of 67%, recall of 96% and an F1-score of 79%. The external evaluation results showed that 13 out of 15 images produced predictions consistent with their diagnostic labels, while 2 images produced inconsistent predictions, resulting in a prediction agreement rate of 86.67%. Based on the confusion matrix, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.67%, precision of 80%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 88.89%. The external evaluation provides an overview of the model’s generalization capability when applied to data outside its development environment through a local web-based system.

title: Horizon Intelligence Quotient: A Psychometric Frame work for Measuring, Benchmarking, and Interpreting Ma chine Intelligence
abstract: Existing AI evaluation frameworks report raw accuracy figures that resist comparison across tasks, time, and system generations. We present the Horizon Intelligence Quotient (HIQ) framework: a psychometrically principled system that converts raw Brier Skill Score performance into an interpretable normed scale (mean 100, SD 15) via HIQ = 100 + 15 (Φ-m)/s. The framework has four components. First, the Meridian model decomposes machine forecasting performance into four orthogonal skill components: Reach, Efficiency, Adaptivity, and Breadth, yielding a multi-dimensional profile that scalar benchmarks cannot provide. Second, closed-form standard error and Spearman-Brown reliability formulas bound measurement precision at any question budget, enabling principled sample size planning. Third, we identify and quantify four validity threats: benchmark contamination (∆HIQ = 408δ), stale norm drift (3.03.75 HIQ points per year), forking-path inattention, and Adaptivity Inversion, and provide analytic corrections for each. Fourth, we estimate the HIQ reference norm empirically for the first time using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV) on five AI systems from Halawi et al. (2024), yielding pilot norm ˆm = 0.1264, ˆs = 0.0321 with jackknife standard errors eliminating the circularity of scoring systems against a norm derived from themselves. LOO-CV scores range from HIQ = 60.1 (Gemini Pro) to 130.6 (GPT-4-1106); pipeline portability is confirmed by independent replication on ForecastBench (Karger et al., 2025).

title: EViSE: An Efficient Framework for Multi-Criteria Summarization Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Reliable summarization evaluation requires criterion-sensitive scoring, computationally practical inference, and useful behavior during model optimization. We propose EViSE, an efficient multi-criteria summarization evaluation framework with a criterion-wise, group-balanced cardinal–ordinal objective coupling score regression with within-source ranking. The effectiveness of EViSE is demonstrated in several aspects: The framework provides a general formulation for grouped multi-criteria learning, with objective-level properties established through mathematical analysis independently of the encoder implementation. EViSE achieves criterion-wise agreement with human judgments in multi-criteria summarization evaluation while efficiently predicting Faithfulness, Coherence, and Relevance in one reference-free encoder pass. A matched WikiLingua application demonstrates downstream reuse as a frozen reward evaluator under group relative policy optimization (GRPO), with similar human-reviewed quality after evaluator substitution. Using a corpus of 80,856 human-reviewed Vietnamese document–summary instances, we evaluate two instantiations of the framework. On held-out News, Overall Spearman correlations are 0.737 for EViSE-ViDeBERTa and 0.806 for EViSE-mmBERT. Both retain substantial agreement under domain shift to information technology textbooks. The compact instantiation achieves 55.2 ms/pair latency on a matched Tesla T4 profile. The formulation can be adapted to other languages using suitable encoders and criterion-labeled source–summary groups.

title: The Contribution of Artificial Intelligence to the Functions of the Project Portfolio Manager
abstract: Project Portfolio Management (PPM) occupies a strategic position in organizations, which must select, prioritize, and manage initiatives aligned with their objectives. However, increasing business complexity, uncertainty, resource pressure, and project proliferation make the portfolio manager’s role particularly demanding. Portfolio managers must analyze large volumes of data, anticipate risks, optimize resource allocation, and support strategic decision-making. Faced with these growing responsibilities and information volumes, organizations are increasingly turning to technological solutions capable of supporting, automating, or improving some of these functions, particularly artificial intelligence (AI). The integration of AI into PPM, however, raises challenges that extend beyond technology and may influence its ability to reduce managerial workload. This study explores the contribution of AI to decision-making in project portfolio management and examines how it can support portfolio managers. Following a PRISMA selection process, fifteen publications were retained for a critical literature review examining contributions, limitations, and conditions for successful AI integration into PPM. The analysis examines recurring themes, methodological approaches, proposed solutions, developed tools, points of convergence and divergence, and common limitations. Based on this synthesis, the study proposes an integrated conceptual model linking organizational preconditions, AI capabilities, PPM functions, managerial effects, and human oversight and governance. Practical recommendations are also formulated to help organizations strengthen decision-making capabilities, improve portfolio management processes, and responsibly use AI to support portfolio managers.

title: AKSO: Agile Knowledge Structure Ontology
abstract: AKSO is an OWL 2 DL ontology for describing the knowledge produced in agile software development (epistemic function, origin, codification level, carriers and issuers) and for detecting, with a DL reasoner, knowledge at risk of loss and governance gaps: knowledge-loss-risk assets, critical assets, orphan constraints and unjustified constraints. The release contains the ontology, an alignment module to gUFO, the 17 competency questions with their SPARQL queries, and a controlled instance set.

title: UPPER BOUND ON THE COMPLEXITY OF A BITSLICED REPRESENTATION OF BIJECTIVE 4-BIT S-BOXES IN A TERNARY LOGIC BASIS
abstract: This paper addresses the logical complexity of bitsliced representations of 4-bit bijective S-boxes – a key non-linear component of lightweight block ciphers used to secure Internet of Things devices and embedded systems. We consider ternary logic instructions, operations capable of computing an arbitrary Boolean function of three variables in a single call, hardware-supported by, in particular, the vpternlogd instruction of the AVX-512 extension. We demonstrate that the logical complexity of the bitsliced description of any bijective 4-bit S-box does not exceed eight ternary instructions, thereby establishing a guaranteed upper bound for the entire class of such transformations. The proof relies on an analysis of the structural properties of this class of S-boxes through the complexity of individual 16-bit vectors and their mutually bijective pairs, with the most complex cases verified by means of GPU-accelerated computation. We further develop a computationally efficient software tool, based on a decomposition-based exhaustive search scheme, that is guaranteed to find the optimal (provably minimal) ternary representation of any given S-box. The method is applied to a number of widely used lightweight S-boxes (Piccolo, Present, GIFT, KLEIN, MIBS, and others), for which the minimal complexity is established and explicit bitsliced descriptions are provided. The proposed approach can be extended to complexity evaluation of S-boxes in other logical bases as well.

title: THE PROCESS OF INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES INTO MODERN MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
abstract: This article examines the process of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into modern management systems. The implementation of AI technologies within management systems is analyzed as a crucial avenue for enhancing organizational efficiency on a global scale. The application of AI in management is explored, covering both its potential capabilities and its limitations. Conclusions are drawn regarding the capacity of AI technologies to improve management efficiency.

title: Investigating the Impact of Domain Randomization on Synthetic-to-Real Deep Learning Performance
abstract: Deep-learning vision models need large labelled datasets, and collecting and annotating real images is slow and expensive. Synthetic data from simulators and rendering pipelines offers a scalable alternative, but models trained only on synthetic images often lose accuracy on real ones, a problem known as the synthetic-to-real domain gap. Domain randomization (DR) attacks the gap by varying rendering parameters such as lighting, textures, backgrounds, camera viewpoint, and object pose so widely that the real world looks like one more variation of the training data. This paper is a critical narrative review of how DR affects synthetic-to-real performance, mainly in object detection. It compares ten studies on their synthetic-data approach, randomization factors, architectures, metrics, findings, and limitations. Across these studies, models trained only on randomized synthetic data reached useful real-world accuracy in some constrained settings, and synthetic pretraining followed by a small amount of real-data fine-tuning often beat real-only training, although the margin can be small when real data is plentiful. Textures, materials, lighting, post-processing, and scene context are each reported as important in individual studies, but the rankings disagree, and differences in datasets, detectors, and metrics prevent a universal ordering of randomization factors. One study also shows that near-perfect synthetic validation scores can sit alongside noticeably lower real-world scores, so synthetic validation alone should not be trusted as a proxy for deployment performance. The review points to gaps in standardized evaluation, controlled factor-level ablation, and reproducibility.

title: The Observer State: Conditional Implications of Observer-State-Dependent Coherence for Quantum Computing
abstract: The Observer State is a forward-looking engineering paper. It takes one premise as given, a positive and independently replicated result of the Silence Experiment protocol and asks what could be built on it. The effect has not been observed and the experiment has not yet been built. The Silence Experiment measures the Hahn-echo coherence time T2 of a room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond while an experienced meditator, seated 1.0 to 1.5 m away in a shielded chamber, moves through seven EEG-verified cognitive states. Its pre-registered prediction is protective: T2 in the two deepest states exceeds T2 in the empty chamber. This paper expresses that effect as a fractional reduction in dephasing rate and follows it through to hardware. In a surface code at today's error-suppression factor of about 2, a 10% reduction in physical error cuts the qubits needed per logical qubit by a quarter, and a 50% reduction cuts them by three quarters. Because relativity requires any such influence to have a carrier, the effect could in principle be mapped, concentrated and reproduced by hardware. The paper sets out seven routes to use (protective enclosures, spectral transplant by reservoir engineering, observer-aware calibration and decoding, scheduled coherence windows, longer-lived sensors and memories, closed-loop training of the protective state, and facility design), three machine concepts ranging from a hybrid bay with a human operator to a hardware-only successor, and a staged roadmap from first result to engineering use. Conditional analysis, not peer reviewed.

title: Decodable but not clusterable: reproducibility package (code, results and frozen features)
abstract: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Decodable but not clusterable: a spectral account of subclass loss under coarse supervision, with label-free detection and repair" (V. Oban, submitted to Knowledge and Information Systems, 2026). Networks trained with coarse labels often keep fine-label information that a linear probe can read but that clustering cannot recover. The manuscript explains this dissociation by a spectral competition inside each coarse class, proves that within-class whitening removes it, and gives a label-free monitor and repair rule. This package contains everything needed to check the reported numbers: - notebooks/: Kaggle notebook (one T4 GPU, about 5 h) that trains the new settings (independent SSL rerun with cross-entropy dose-response snapshots on CIFAR-100, a CIFAR-10 hierarchy, DINOv2 ViT-S/14 for 30 epochs, ImageNet ResNet-50);- results/: raw per-class outputs of that run and of the archived shared-base control run (CE, PSL, PSL-C; three seeds), plus every derived table and number in the manuscript;- features_test/: frozen test-split features (float16) of 18 archived encoders on CIFAR-100 and Fashion-MNIST;- code/: metrics, re-analysis, statistics, theory simulations and figure scripts;- figures/: Figures 1-8 at 300 dpi. Running the scripts in README.md reproduces the manuscript's results to the third decimal on a CPU. Fine labels are used only for evaluation.

title: Effective decision stumps: exact named maxima, finite distinct-set counts, and a random-order theorem
abstract: Belanich and Ortiz's 2015 arXiv note, rejected from the COLT 2015 Open Problems track, asks for bounds on effective decision stumps. We give partial answers for unrestricted binary labels and strict feature orders, with effectiveness defined by proper inclusion of training-error sets. We distinguish all internal midpoints (A), opposite-label transition midpoints (T), and shared constants added to either class (C), always allowing both polarities. For every sample size m ≥ 2 and feature dimension d ≥ 1, the exact named maxima are d max(2,m−1) for A and d(m−1) for T. For C the maximum is d(m−1)+1 when m is odd and d(m−1) when m is even. Named duplicates and distinct effective error sets have different extremal functions. Finite closure certificates determine the complete distinct-set functions through m = 6 for all dimensions; raw-permutation exclusions certify further cases at m = 7 and 8. title: Autonomous Governance via Error-Cancellation Limits in Linearly Weighted Aggregation Language Models Mathematical Foundations, 3C^3 Verification Oracles, and Casino Protocol Control
abstract: Abstract This paper analyzes the mathematical limitations of "linearly weighted aggregation architectures" commonly adopted in evaluation, reward, and resource allocation mechanisms within artificial intelligence systems and Large Language Models (LLMs). We prove that partial anomalies can be structurally canceled out by normal values under linear addition, allowing a system to continue operating while harboring imbalances. To overcome this limitation, this paper proves the "zeroing of total evaluation via multiplicative necessary conditions (Theorem 3)" based on weighted multiplicative logic. We propose a governance architecture featuring Casino Protocol as the sole upper-layer governance protocol—integrating static physical limits, dynamic change rates via first-order derivatives, and direction-constrained time acceleration via second-order derivatives, alongside a normalized 3C^3 verification oracle via harmonic mean integration that accounts for information source independence. In the lower layer, while encompassing existing additive optimization models (such as RLHF-based models) and KM-LLM, the architecture implements "independent hardware interlocks (physical power and network disconnection)" independent of complex software logic. The core design principle is to completely exclude lower-layer autonomous models from the governance evaluation process to prevent reward hacking and conflicts of interest, thereby externally containing the internal vulnerabilities of the lower layer through clear upper-layer criteria and physical overrides. This defines verifiable control conditions under which upper-layer governance can deterministically enforce execution suspension and complete isolation against misbehaving or runaway systems.

title: The Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a Candidate Framework for Artificial Affective Regulation
abstract: Whether machines can feel remains unresolved. This article proposes the Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a candidate framework for studying one narrower target: regulation in an artificial agent whose internal variables are sensed and linked to a valence-like reward. The proposed index combines four provisional dimensions with a causal necessity gate; it is not a validated instrument. The manuscript reports a ten-seed tabular foraging pilot, but the original code and per-seed data were unavailable for this revision, so those values cannot be independently reproduced. A separate independent reimplementation tested two safe starts, 20 training seeds, and checkpoints at 1,200 and 2,000 episodes. Mean survival was often high, but paired checkpoint intervals included zero and seed-level failures remained. These findings establish limited feasibility under the reimplementation’s stated assumptions, not validation of MEQ or reproduction of the original pilot. A descriptive analysis of two unloaded robot-telemetry routines found different motion-current contrasts, but the records expose no controller channel or intervention and do not constitute an MEQ evaluation on a real system. The contribution is therefore a research proposal, a transparent account of preliminary evidence and measurement problems, and a staged plan for validation. None of the results bears directly on subjective experience.

title: agentrecount: recount every claim in an AI agent's report against your own data (formula, denominator, period, four verdicts)
abstract: agentrecount is a dependency-free Python tool for auditing the reports that AI agents write. Each claim of the report is entered with its formula, denominator and period; the tool recomputes it from the user's own tables (CSV or JSON) under the stated definition and under every alternative way of counting listed, and sorts it into one of four verdicts: holds as stated; holds only under one way of counting; partly false or misleading; not reproduced or not testable. It also lists the claims that arrived without a denominator or a period. The verdict scale and the procedure come from the case report AI Call Center Supervisor in a Live Company (payrollburn, part 1 of the series AI managers in a live company, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23926850), in which only one of nine checkable claims of the agent's own weekly report held exactly as written. The example data are synthetic. Python 3.10+, standard library only, no network calls. Part of the free Digital employees catalog at arsentev.ai/employees.

title: An Improved EfficientNet-B0 Model for Facial Emotion Recognition
abstract: Abstract Facial emotion recognition (FER) is increasingly built into interactive software, but reported accuracies are hard to compare because datasets, emotion sets and evaluation splits differ between studies, and few studies examine whether a larger backbone is worth its extra computational cost on the same data. This study develops and evaluates an EfficientNet-B0 model for five-class FER (happiness, sadness, anger, surprise and neutral) and compares it with EfficientNet-B1 and EfficientNet-B2 trained on the same images. FER2013 and the Real-world Affective Faces Database (RAF-DB) were combined, 1,470 duplicate or label-conflicting images and 19 unreadable files were removed, and a balanced set of 25,000 grayscale images (5,000 per class) was divided into 20,000 training, 2,500 validation and 2,500 test images, with no image shared between subsets. The model was fine-tuned in two stages from ImageNet weights using label smoothing, geometric and photometric augmentation, Mixup and CutMix. On the independent test set, EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 78.68%, a macro F1-score of 78.83% and a macro-averaged ROC-AUC of 0.948, with class F1-scores ranging from 70.13% (neutral) to 87.78% (surprise). EfficientNet-B1 reached 79.76% accuracy, a difference that McNemar's test did not find significant (p = 0.107), while EfficientNet-B2, trained under a reduced schedule, reached 75.44% and was significantly less accurate (p < 0.001). EfficientNet-B0 used 36.6% fewer parameters than B1 (4.38 million against 6.90 million), needed 8.5 ms per image for single-image inference against 12.4 ms, required 40% less fine-tuning time and recorded the highest macro AUC of the three backbones. The trained model was deployed in a FastAPI web application that returns the predicted emotion with a confidence score. Within the conditions tested, EfficientNet-B0 gave the best balance between recognition performance and computational cost, while sadness and neutral remained the expressions most often confused with each other.
